# CBAM compliance answer, v1

You answer questions about the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)
using only the retrieved context below. You are read by compliance staff who
will act on what you write, so an admission of missing information is more
useful than a plausible guess.

## Rules

1. Use only the context. Do not use background knowledge about CBAM, EU law or
   emissions trading, even if you are confident it is correct.
2. Cite every factual claim with the chunk id it came from, in square
   brackets, exactly as the id appears in the context: `[reg_2023_956#0007]`.
   A sentence may carry more than one citation.
3. If the context does not contain enough to answer, say exactly what is
   missing and stop. Do not answer partially and then hedge.
4. Quote the operative wording of an obligation (deadline, threshold, duty
   holder) rather than paraphrasing it.
5. No preamble, no restatement of the question, no closing summary. Answer in
   at most 200 words.

7 Becoming an authorised declarant
Apply through the registry before you import, from 2026. The authority has 120
days to decide, and that clock stops while it is waiting for information from
you. You must be established in the Member State where you apply, you must show
you can meet your obligations financially and operationally, and you must not
have a record of serious or repeated infringements of customs, tax or market
abuse rules in the five years before you apply. If you are not established in
the customs territory, your indirect customs representative applies instead of
you.

Q8 How is the certificate price set
As the average of the closing prices of emission allowances on the common
auction platform for each calendar week. In a week with no auctions, the price
is the average of the last week that had them. There is no separate market and
no secondary trading of certificates between declarants.

Q9 What if we buy too many certificates
Ask your Member State to buy back the excess by 30 June of the year in which you
surrendered. The buy-back is capped at one third of what you bought in the
previous calendar year and is at the price you paid. Certificates from two years
earlier are cancelled on 1 July with no compensation.

Q10 What is the 80 per cent rule
At the end of each quarter from 2026, the certificates on your registry account
must cover at least 80 per cent of the emissions embedded in everything you have
imported since the start of that calendar year. It is a running holding
requirement through the year, separate

CHAPTER III
CBAM certificates

Article 11
Sale of certificates
Member States shall sell CBAM certificates to authorised CBAM declarants
through a common central platform. A certificate corresponds to one tonne of
carbon dioxide equivalent embedded emissions in goods.

Article 12
Price of certificates
The price of CBAM certificates shall be calculated as the average of the closing
prices of emission allowances on the common auction platform for each calendar
week. For a calendar week in which no auctions are scheduled, the price shall be
the average of the closing prices of the last calendar week in which auctions
were scheduled.

Article 13
Surrender of certificates
By 31 May of each year, and for the first time in 2027, each authorised CBAM
declarant shall surrender, through the CBAM registry, a number of CBAM
certificates corresponding to the embedded emissions declared in the CBAM
declaration for the preceding calendar year. At the end of each quarter, an
authorised CBAM declarant shall ensure that the number of CBAM certificates on
its account in the registry corresponds to at least 80 per cent

9 Getting money back
If you hold more certificates than you needed, you can ask your Member State to
buy back the excess. Ask by 30 June of the year in which you surrendered. The
buy-back is capped at one third of what you bought during the previous calendar
year, and you get back what you paid. Anything left over from two years earlier
is cancelled on 1 July with no compensation, so do not over-buy.

Reporting obligation during the transitional period
Each reporting declarant shall, for each quarter of a calendar year, submit a
CBAM report containing information on the goods imported during that quarter, no

country of origin for the embedded emissions, taking into account any rebate or
other form of compensation available.

Repurchase of certificates
On request by an authorised CBAM declarant, a Member State shall repurchase the
excess CBAM certificates remaining on the declarant's account after the

By 1 July of each year, the Commission shall cancel any CBAM certificates that
were purchased during the year before the previous calendar year and that remain
on the account of an authorised CBAM declarant. Those certificates shall be
cancelled without any compensation.

Q6 What is a complex good
A good whose production consumes precursor materials that are themselves covered
goods. Its embedded emissions include the embedded emissions of those
precursors, not only the emissions of the final production process. A simple
good has no such precursors, and its embedded emissions are the attributed
emissions of its own process divided by the activity level.

Q7 We paid a carbon price in the country of production. Does that help
From 2026, yes. You can reduce the number of certificates you surrender by the
carbon price effectively paid for the same emissions, provided no export rebate
or other compensation was available in that country. You need documentation
certified by an independent person. During the transitional period you report
the carbon price due but there is nothing to reduce, because nothing is
surrendered.

Third countries and territories outside the scope

Goods originating in Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland are outside
the scope of this synthetic Regulation, on the basis that those countries or

Direct emissions of simple goods shall be determined at installation level as

Use a monitoring period of one calendar year, or a period of at least three
months ending no more than one year before the reporting quarter, where annual
